label: Youth suicide rate (ages 15-24)
reliability_criteria: Canonical tier = Eurostat's causes-of-death crude death rate for intentional self-harm (ICD-10 X60-X84, Y87.0) at ages 15-24, both sexes, per 100,000 persons: the national civil-registration death registers as collected by Eurostat from the national statistical offices, 36 countries, 2011-2023, the collector's own per-observation flags transported as-reported. High for the countries it covers, with one caveat: in small countries (Liechtenstein, Malta, Iceland, Cyprus, Luxembourg) a handful of deaths moves the rate by several points from one year to the next. No witness tier wired: the WHO Global Health Estimates print youth suicide on other bands (15-19, 15-29) for a single 2021 cross-section of 185 countries, modeled (SDGSUICIDE age slices) - recorded, not wired.
license: Mixed, per source (see "sources"): Eurostat reuse policy (attribution required, no endorsement implied).
notes: Deaths by intentional self-harm per 100,000 young people aged 15 to 24, outside Todd's books (the all-ages rate, suicide_rate, is Todd's 2nd metric by citations). The crude rate is not age-standardized within the band. THE HONEST LIMITS: the coverage is the European club (the same ceiling as the other Eurostat collectors); the band 15-24 differs from the WHO estimates' 15-29 / 15-19 bands; the reclassification caveat of suicide applies (an undetermined-intent death is not counted as self-harm).
